simple.meaning: נָקִיק (nâqîyq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a cleft.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Isaiah 7:19. Its contexts include mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָקִיק (H5357).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָקִיק (nâqîyq) / H5357 is traced through Isaiah 7:19, Jeremiah 13:4, Jeremiah 16:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5357. naqiq [ נָקִיק ] noun masculine cleft of rock ; — only construct: singular הַסָּ֑לַע נְקִיק Jer 13:4 ; plural הַסְּלָעִים נְקִיקֵי Isa 7:19 (|| הַבַּתּוֺת נַחֲלֵי ), Jer 16:16 .
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to bore ;

occurrences.englishText: They shall come, and shall all rest in the desolate valleys, in the clefts of the rocks, on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures.
“Take the belt that you have bought, which is on your waist, and arise, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a cleft of the rock.”

“Behold, I will send for many fishermen,” says Yahweh, “and they will fish them up. Afterward I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every mountain, from every hill, and out of the clefts of the rocks.
